All three render clearly. Here are the three ways of adding tags — the review card is otherwise identical, and each shows the same result once saved (tags as pills, plus your personal note in the highlighted band). Screenshots are under `prototypes/`.

**Option A — type a tag, press Enter** (`shot-06-tags-optionA.png`)
Each tag becomes a little removable pill as you type it and press Enter (or comma). Click the × to drop one. Clean and unambiguous; each tag is visibly its own thing.

**Option B — one comma-separated field** (`shot-07-tags-optionB.png`)
You type all your tags in a single box separated by commas (`reading, focus, weekend-writing`). Fastest to type in one go, but tags aren't shown as separate pills while you edit.

**Option C — tap a suggestion or type your own** (`shot-08-tags-optionC.png`)
Same pill behaviour as A, but it also offers tags **you've used before** as one-tap suggestions underneath, so your tag names stay consistent over time (helpful later when you're searching). You can still type brand-new ones.

For the **note**, all three treat it the same way: a separate "Your note — why you saved it" field, kept distinct from the page's own description, and shown on the saved card in the highlighted band.

**Which tag-entry approach feels most natural to you — A, B, or C?** (If you like C's reuse-your-past-tags idea but prefer a different feel, tell me and I'll blend it.) And separately: does keeping your **note** as its own thing, apart from the page description, match how you think about "why I saved this"?
